title: Davis–Kahan rotation of eigenvectors
abstract: Formalizes the sin-Theta, tan-Theta, sin-two-Theta, and tan-two-Theta theorem families from Section 2 of Davis and Kahan (1970), for real or complex separable Hilbert spaces, including common-domain unbounded operators and symmetric-norm estimates. The tan-Theta endpoint requires Rayleigh–Ritz trial data with residual orthogonal to the trial subspace.

informal.RotationOfEigenvectors.sinTheta_mem_and_: With finite symmetric residual norm, a spectral gap gives sine-angle ideal membership and controls its symmetric norm by the corresponding residual norm.
informal.RotationOfEigenvectors.tanTheta: For Rayleigh–Ritz trial data with residual orthogonal to the trial subspace, a positive directed spectral gap between the trial compression and the unwanted reducing block gives the symmetric-norm tangent-angle residual estimate and tangent pole exclusion, assuming the residual has finite symmetric norm.
informal.RotationOfEigenvectors.sinTwoTheta_direc: Under the printed oriented gap and common-domain self-adjointness hypotheses, finite symmetric residual norm gives directed sine-double-angle ideal membership, and twice the residual norm bounds the gap times its norm.
informal.RotationOfEigenvectors.sinTwoTheta_ambie: Finite symmetric perturbation norm gives ambient sine-double-angle ideal membership and the whole-space gap bound under the theorem's reducing and perturbed-gap hypotheses.
informal.RotationOfEigenvectors.tanTwoTheta: The residual tangent-double-angle estimate holds with the theorem’s source-facing block hypotheses.
